nodes.summary: There exist an entire function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and two distinct straight lines $l \ne m$ in $\mathbb{C}$ such that every zero of $f$ lies on $l$, every solution of $f(z) = 1$ lies on $m$, and $f$ has infinitely many zeros and infinitely many solutions of $f(z) = 1$. Here a straight line is a set $\{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ with $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ and $v \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Entire functions with zeros and ones on two distinct lines exist

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there exist an entire function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and two distinct straight lines $l \ne m$ in $\mathbb{C}$ such that every zero of $f$ lies on $l$, every solution of $f(z) = 1$ lies on $m$, and $f$ has infinitely many zeros and infinitely many solutions of $f(z) = 1$. Here a straight line is a set $\{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$ with $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ and $v \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Zeros and ones of an entire function on two distinct lines

nodes.summary: A set $s \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a straight line if there are $a, v \in \mathbb{C}$ with $v \ne 0$ such that $s = \{a + tv : t \in \mathbb{R}\}$.
nodes.title: Straight lines in the complex plane

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has all its ones in a set $m \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ if every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = 1$ lies in $m$.
nodes.title: Functions whose ones lie in a given set

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has all its zeros in a set $l \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ if every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = 0$ lies in $l$.
nodes.title: Functions whose zeros lie in a given set
